notes: Predicate tree nodes exactly as parser.parse emits: ('cmp', name, op, literal), ('and', l, r), ('or', l, r), ('not', child). node=None evaluates True (no WHERE). Ops: '=', '!=', '<', '<=', '>', '>='. Comparison where either side is None yields False for every operator except '!=' which yields True. Missing column raises KeyError(name). filter_rows(node, table) returns ascending row indices of a tinyq.schema.Table satisfying node, using table.nrows() and table.row(i); node=None returns all indices. No dependencies imported at runtime: predicate.py is pure stdlib and only consumes the tuple tree shape plus the Table row/nrows protocol.
